subject: Stepwise commit staircase and fallback burst pocket for Q4
messages:
From: Oliver Chen <oliver@edgesupply.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Sep 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API commit: Q4 traffic spike + temporary burst request

Hey Priya / Karthik,

Quick context: we run EdgeSupply search + recommendation flows through Redwood hosted API. Based on our summer tests and Q4 forecast, we expect a user-driven spike in November and December (holiday vertical). Today we're on a 2M monthly commit and a modest burst window; we want to formalize a short staircase to reach 5M/mo by November and have a fallback burst pocket for unexpected peaks.

Specific asks:
- Proposal for a stepwise commit: Sept -> Oct -> Nov (e.g., 2M -> 3M -> 5M) with pro-rata billing for the ramp month
- A defined burst pocket (1.5x commit, limited to X tokens/day) and how soft-throttle vs hard-throttle behaves once burst is consumed
- Confirmation of p95 latency SLO (we aim for <=150ms p95 for generate calls) and any recommended model variants to hit cost/latency goals
- Updated SOW and timeline so procurement can sign (we're aiming to finalize by 9/15)

I've attached our usage history for July-August to help sizing. Looping in procurement shortly.

Thanks,
Oliver
Sr. Platform Engineer
EdgeSupply, Inc.

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver@edgesupply.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Sep 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit: Q4 traffic spike + temporary burst request

Thanks for the clear ask, Oliver — this matches patterns we see for seasonal clients. I pulled together a pragmatic ramp we can operationalize quickly and an SOW draft attached. High level proposal: 

- Commit staircase (monthly committed tokens): Sep 2028: 2.0M (existing) | Oct 2028: 3.0M | Nov 2028 onward: 5.0M
- Burst pocket: 1.5x of the active monthly commit (applies as daily burst budget, capped at a rolling 7-day window)
- Billing: pro-rata for Oct (partial month ramp), standard monthly invoice on the 1st following the ramp month; we can accept PO prior to the Nov effective commit if procurement prefers
- Latency SLO: hosted p95 target 150ms for our fast-gen model; if you need stricter latency we can propose a dedicated capacity add-on (we kept this as optional)
- Model variants: suggest primary served model x-redwood-fast and fallback x-redwood-quant (slightly cheaper with similar quality) for controlled cost during bursts

Next steps: if the staircase above is acceptable, we'll: 1) finalize SOW (attached) 2) generate DocuSign envelope for signatures 3) schedule an ops handoff with Karthik to confirm rate limits and fallback behavior. Please confirm procurement contact and PO cadence so Lauren and I can prepare the billing lane.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Account Director, Redwood Inference

---

On Tue, 11 Sep 2028 11:15:00 -0700, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks — quick ops notes to clarify how the burst/fallback will behave from a runtime perspective:
>
> - Rate limits: per-route soft limit 120 requests/min with per-token gating at the token-level bucket; soft limit allows graceful shedding but preserves high-priority requests; hard limit will reject beyond configured hard threshold (we recommend hard threshold at ~2x average sustained rps)
> - Autoscaling: hosted autoscale will provision additional inference capacity within the same region; typical spin-up latency under our fast-path kernel selection is ~45-90s depending on model size
> - Fallback model variant: during sustained burst consumption we'll automatically route to x-redwood-quant (quantized 8-bit) after a configurable CPU/GPU load threshold to reduce cost and preserve throughput; KV cache and prefix caching remain active so session coherence is preserved
> - Observability: we'll enable per-route token-level cost breakdown and set a regression alert for quality drift tied to a small eval prompt set you provide
>
> I'll coordinate an ops runbook draft after SOW sign-off and include throttling behavior examples (what a client sees at p99 when burst is exhausted).
>
> — Karthik
> Principal Engineer, Runtime
>
